description: The Spaarke PRODUCT configuration tables that 'Spaarke Core User' and 'Spaarke Basic User' read at Global (Organization) depth (owner decision 2026-10-29, BU1 move plan Q1). Spaarke product data is owned in the root business unit (owner round 136), and people work in a customer business unit below it. A Read at Deep reaches only the user's own unit and its children, so a user outside the root reads none of the root's product rows (measured on spaarkedev1 with RetrievePrincipalAccess: a user in a child unit had no access to root-owned grid configuration, playbook and AI tool type rows). Read at Global on these tables only closes that gap. Nothing else changes: no Write, Create, Delete, Append, AppendTo, Assign or Share, and no other role. The source of truth is the solution role XML (src/dataverse/solutions/SpaarkeMaster/Roles/Spaarke Core User.xml and Spaarke Basic User.xml), which ships the change to every environment; this file is the ONE declared list of the tables. tests/Spaarke.ArchTests/ProductConfigurationReadRoleGuardTests.cs checks that both role files hold each listed Read at Global and that no listed table is customer data; scripts/Set-ProductConfigurationReadDepth.ps1 applies the list to one environment ahead of a solution import and verifies it.
howToExtend: Add a table only when it holds Spaarke product configuration that every user must read wherever their business unit sits: a seeded catalog, playbook building block or UI configuration with no customer content and no per-user rows. Give it a reason and the read-only evidence that it is product configuration.

Never add a customer record table or anything holding customer content. ProductConfigurationReadRoleGuardTests fails the build for: a hard-deny table (RecordOwnershipResolver.RestrictedContentTables), an ownership parent (RecordOwnershipResolver.OwnershipParentEntities), a secure root or secure-child table (SecureChildLineage), a table in config/secure-record-owner-role.json (the census guards those), a customer configuration table (config/customer-configuration-owner-role.json), and a per-user table (OwnedChildWrite.PerUserTables).
Change the role XML in the same commit: both role files must hold the table's Read at Global, or the guard fails.

'privilegeName' is the Read privilege's name from metadata (EntityDefinitions(LogicalName='x')/Privileges, PrivilegeType eq 'Read'). The casing follows the schema name. The script checks it against metadata and refuses a mismatch.
A table considered and left out goes in 'excluded' with its reason, so the decision is not re-litigated. The guard keeps 'tables' and 'excluded' disjoint.

Then run scripts/Set-ProductConfigurationReadDepth.ps1 -EnvironmentUrl <url> (dry run), -Apply (owner go), then -Verify, on each environment that will not get the change from a SpaarkeMaster import first.
